reviewerNotes.developmentRuns: Before this recorded run, the reviewer ran single sections of the same script while it was written (logs not kept). Those runs failed only on reviewer script errors: locators that ran before a list loaded, a Tab key that stays inside a date input, a Portal link query that also matched the Your requests list, a counterparty answer that the Convert dialog carries by design, and an API response shape. They left extra records named DOC-029 admin-config with other suffixes (mu49dyo7, mu49gs2n, mu49ogjv, mu49zjk4, mu4a758i, mu4aajaz, mu4ae1f0, mu4ah3e4, mu4ajt1o, mu4anzu9, mu4atdhb, mu4azgv6) and one Entity named DOC-029 admin-config Officer Holdings probe. The recorded run (suffix mu4b3b28) removed the development runs' deflection links and turned off Portal-listed on their Entities. Organisation lead times were restored to the recorded list after each run.
observations: The Reminder lead times page note still reads 'One list covers every tracked date'. The article says a Contract or Matter Key date can add its own lead times, and the walkthrough saw the own 12-day lead time fire. The article matches the behaviour; the page note is out of date.
Archive type with 'No reassignment' on an in-use Matter type leaves the dialog open with no message. Nothing changes, so the refusal is silent.
The Field archive dialog counted a Field attached to one type with one stored value as 'attached to 2 types'.
The request type archive dialog says the type 'is not used by any requests' while Requests still name it, and shows a disabled 'Reassign requests to' select. The article describes this.
With a long Field catalog the Attach field menu opened taller than the 900 px viewport and its top items were above the screen. The script chose menu items with the keyboard.
No seeded Entity in the admin lab is Portal-listed, so a required Entity Field on a Portal form offers only Not set until an Administrator turns on Portal-listed.
limitations: Independent agent walkthrough, not a human user study.
The bell contents were read from GET /api/v1/notifications as the colleague; the browser checked only the header bell count.
The morning round was queued in the lab worker through pg-boss on the real clock; no clock change.

Not checked in the browser: requiredness at type change; every Stage or Category keeping a live Status; failed multi-part Field saves; the AI prompt and AI preparation; renaming and reordering request types; Department carry-through; a turnaround of 0 meaning the submission date; Key date reorder in a template; a template section failing after an earlier section saved (the editor refuses invalid rows before any section saves); expiry, notice deadline and Entity Obligation reminders; Search not covering record content.
The archived-target check set a request type Target through PATCH /api/v1/request-types/<id>, because the editor has no Target control.
